title: fix(ui): allow oversized PNG attachments
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: chat rejects an oversized PNG dropped into the composer instead of preparing a smaller image for upload.

## User Impact

Users can drop, pick, or paste oversized static PNGs in chat and New Session. The browser resizes them to the Gateway-advertised byte limit while preserving aspect ratio and transparency; already-small files remain unchanged. No server limit or configuration changes are required.

Resizing supports static PNG sources up to 25 megapixels. Animated PNGs are not silently flattened, and other formats retain their existing limits. Failed preparation remains visible and does not send oversized bytes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preparation stays inside the shared attachment lifecycle, preserving pending-send, cancellation, ordering, and destination ownership. A disposable browser worker owns decoding, drawing, and encoding; jobs are serialized to bound pixel memory. Queue waits do not consume another image's processing timeout. Pasted image data also avoids a costly per-byte string-iterator callback.

## Evidence

- Real Chromium regression failed before the fix through drop, picker, and image-data paste; the repaired paths preserve PNG transparency and publish matching, bounded payload bytes.
- 226 focused tests passed across attachment ingestion, chat/New Session composers, typing, cancellation, and pane handoff. A fake-clock regression also proves two individually valid 10-second/6-second jobs do not time out because they were queued.
- Independent review: no actionable P0–P2 findings after repairs. Selected type, format, lint, i18n, ownership, and dead-export checks were exercised; the production UI bundle includes the worker.
- Secretless, network-none real-browser performance matrix: single ~6 MB PNG, six-file batch, near-25 MP PNG, image-data paste, both composers, normal and 4× renderer CPU slowdown. All 1,680 typed characters matched their drafts, retained order/focus, and no page errors occurred. Active/queued cancellation and context switching preserved attachment ownership.

| Measured operation | Before | Final candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| PNG drawing/encoding on the composer thread | Up to 149 ms near 25 MP at 4× | No main-thread drawing/encoding calls |
| ~6 MB data-URL paste handler, normal CPU | 268 ms | 20 ms |
| ~6 MB data-URL paste handler, 4× CPU | 1,056 ms | 68 ms |

The original DOM-resize measurements ran on the host; final worker measurements ran in a 4-CPU/8-GiB isolated container, so the first row is an attribution result rather than a controlled percentage-speedup claim. Both paste-handler measurements used the isolated harness. Existing FileReader/composer-rendering spikes remain observable under CPU throttling; this is not a claim of universally hitch-free rendering. Chromium was exercised; other browsers were not live-tested.

The full bundled E2E route was unavailable: host loopback preflight returned HTTP 502, then the supported isolated runtime build was SIGKILLed. The focused actual-UI source harness ran successfully in secretless isolation instead; all owned containers/browser processes were cleaned up.

Test cost: the seven-file focused run took 33.14 seconds wall time with one worker. The new browser file spent 368 ms in tests (1.61 seconds including runner overhead); the updated attachment unit file's final standalone run took 4.07 seconds wall time. The command-palette fixture repair passed all 12 tests in 7.13 seconds wall time (5.99 seconds in Vitest); its combined replay with attachment tests passed all 33 tests in 6.68 seconds. UI test type shards, focused lint, formatting, and an independent P0–P2 review of the repair passed.

CI on initial head 2dfb369b0c88 [failed in checks-ui (1/3)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36358923424/job/108732281702): two cold command-palette fixtures still treated oversized PNGs as synchronous admission rejection. Both failures reproduced locally. The fixtures now use non-resizable GIFs while preserving every no-silent-drop and partial-submit assertion; production code is unchanged. The initial CI attachment test file passed in 0.35 seconds of test execution; the palette file took 1.53 seconds in that failing run. Exact-head CI on e7ee8955bbb235bcbf2f4a734c688d78ce97c908 subsequently [passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36360501989), including openclaw/ci-gate, all three checks-ui shards, all nine checks-ui-e2e shards, Control UI performance, and security review. In the passing UI job, attachment tests took 0.36 seconds and command-palette attachment tests took 2.26 seconds of test execution. ClawSweeper completed its exact-head review with no actionable findings. The local bundled-E2E limitation above remains an accurate account of the local proof route; hosted UI E2E is now green.
